preamble: Genuine insertion of [z] with no etymological source is a narrow, essentially French phenomenon. Ordinary French liaison (les amis [lezami], deux ans [døzɑ̃]) is not ∅→z: it is the resurfacing of a latent final consonant historically present in the word. True insertion occurs where the [z] has no lexical source: the euphonic -s of second-person singular imperatives before the clitics y and en (va → vas-y [vazi], mange → manges-en), and hypercorrect or jocular faulty liaisons (pataquès) such as moi-z-aussi.

examples.from: va [va] 'go!' (2sg imperative of aller, no final -s)
examples.note: Euphonic s: before the clitics y and en the imperative of aller and of first-conjugation verbs takes an -s pronounced [z], which has no etymological source in the imperative form; likewise parles-en 'talk about it', manges-en 'eat some'.
Pataquès: a faulty liaison inserting [z] where no consonant exists, made by hypercorrection or for comic effect; also donne-moi-z-en 'give me some'.
